clue.text: Embassy official gets certificate on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the certificate comes first

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate awarded for a course of study

explanation.surface: A consular worker is handed an official document just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is a state's representative abroad, typically working from an embassy.

clue.text: Man left on river? More than one concerned

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the river

parts.note: a chessman, here the pawn, is written P in chess notation
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a man abandoned beside a river, then a remark about several people being involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is a chess piece: the pawn, P.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the plural form is used where more than one thing is in question.

clue.text: Have convulsions about cheeseparing in cultural expression

indicators.note: the convulsions are placed about, that is around, the stingy word

parts.note: to have fits is to suffer convulsions
near is an old word for mean or stingy, as cheeseparing is

explanation.surface: Someone thrown into spasms by miserliness in the arts world.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR meaning stingy is a sense found mainly in older British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, sculpture and music are the fine arts, the classic forms of cultural expression.

parts.note: something out is unfashionable or not to be considered, hence undesirable
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Starting off with an unwelcome bunch of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the beginning of something, a synonym for the start.

parts.note: C is Cuba's international vehicle registration code
hilly is a milder word for mountainous

explanation.surface: A travel note that Cuba is rugged and inhospitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly reception is a cold, unfriendly one, so the word means unwelcoming.

parts.note: Charlie is the radio alphabet word for C
haste is rash hurry, close to impulsiveness

explanation.surface: Charlie's rashness has been held in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means modest and self-controlled, especially in conduct, so restrained.

clue.text: Private eye turned round to see pretty girls

parts.note: PI is short for private investigator, a private eye

indicators.note: round says the word for turned is brought about to face the other way

parts.note: spun means turned, as a wheel is

explanation.surface: A detective spins about and spots some attractive women.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin-ups are pictures of glamorous models pinned to walls, and by extension the models themselves.

indicators.note: in says the time letter goes inside the club

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club

explanation.surface: Arriving at the club exactly on the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightclub, but it is the golf club once called a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an informal British idiom for exactly right or accurate.

clue.text: Aristocrat to protest over troublesome noises

indicators.note: in a down clue the protest goes over, above, the rest

parts.note: a march is a protest by demonstrators walking together

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters are unruly and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A noblewoman demonstrates against irritating racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is the wife of a marquess or a woman holding that rank, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Visitor found in the bingo hall

definitions.meaning: someone who calls on you at home is a visitor
the person in a bingo hall who announces the numbers drawn

explanation.surface: A guest turns up at the local bingo night.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a person paying a visit and the announcer who reads out bingo numbers.

parts.note: A is the film classification letter for adult
an adaptation of a book or play is a version of it

explanation.surface: A grown-up hates a remake of a favourite story.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong feeling of distaste, a synonym for dislike.

definitions.note: something that is very small, the tiniest particle

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Describing a tiny kitten.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, so a byword for anything minute.

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol or a drug
a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies

explanation.surface: A man called Spike receives his allotted portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name; it is the verb for adding something to a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceration is a tear or gash in the skin, a kind of cut.

clue.text: Six-footer to remain in splinter group

parts.note: to stick is to stay put, remain
a sect is a group that has broken away from a larger body

explanation.surface: A tall person decides to stay loyal to a breakaway faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it means a creature with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick insect, like every insect, has six legs, making it literally a six-footer.

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rodents have chewed holes in some garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's light sleeveless undergarment, an item of clothing.

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
apace means quickly, at speed

explanation.surface: A car going fast turns into an empty husk.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar creature.

indicators.note: a peer who tours something goes around it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A lord travels the streets looking for a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' reads as the animal but is the verb meaning to nag.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag or harass them persistently, a synonym for this verb.

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a deal was in fact refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb meaning in fact or truly, as actually does.

clue.text: Try to stop my old Dutch being resolute

parts.note: to deter someone is to try to put them off doing something
mine is the old form of my, as in mine eyes

explanation.surface: Attempting to halt an elderly Dutch friend who is set on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Dutch' looks like a phrase (cockney slang for a wife), but 'old' goes with 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined means firmly resolved, unwavering in purpose.

indicators.note: first says the quits word comes before the Oscar letter

parts.note: being quits means being square, at evens
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: An actor named Oscar resigns first, despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is an idiom meaning in spite of that, a synonym for nevertheless.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, a parent
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Something to eat for a mother and her offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum, a kind of fruit.

definitions.meaning: a line of soldiers standing side by side

explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a riding track in London's Hyde Park; the question mark flags that the phrase is split.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both foul-smelling and a line of soldiers.

parts.note: at, like in, places something at a location
heists are robberies, especially large ones

explanation.surface: Unbelievers who are mixed up in raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheists are people who do not believe in any god.

indicators.note: breaking the word into fragments lets its letters be reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Try out pieces of wood from a few trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Maples are deciduous trees, the source of maple syrup.

clue.text: Posh student staying in holiday development

indicators.note: the posh student is staying inside the holiday word

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
U means upper-class, posh, in British usage
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An upper-class student stays put in a new holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holiday development' looks like a resort complex, but 'development' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is an outcome, what something develops into, so a development.

clue.text: Contrived to get engineer into car

indicators.note: into says the engineer is put inside the car

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to squeeze a mechanic into a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced means artificial or strained, not natural, as something contrived is.
